request.deadline: Three quarterly milestones over 9 months, July 2026 - March 2027
deliverables: Ongoing maintenance: bug fixes, dependency upkeep, security patches, and releases
Dijkstra developer preview including initial Plutus V4 support in the compiler and standard library
Improved interfaces and documentation for JS/TS components embedded in MeshJS, Evolution SDK, and Lucid Evolution
Dijkstra ledger rules and transaction-builder updates including new builtins, cost models, nested transactions, accounts, and guard scripts
Java/Kotlin integration examples for Spring Boot and Ktor and cleaner integration with Cardano Client Lib and Yaci
Runtime foundational components, reactive workers, chain follower, and task scheduler
request.recipient: Lantr Engineering is named as the team; treasury payment recipient/address is not stated in document.
request.what: Fund a 9-month continuation of Scalus covering maintenance, Dijkstra hard-fork readiness, JVM and JS/TS interoperability, and a scoped application runtime.

claims.claim: Scalus is an established open-source Cardano development platform built by Lantr Engineering over three years of continuous delivery.
Scalus is used directly by Gummiworm L2, Bifrost, SugarRush, Vela, and DID/DIDComm.
Scalus components are reused in MeshJS, Evolution SDK, Lucid Evolution, Cardano Client Lib, and YaciDevKit.
The project has 4,642 commits across 32 releases, 12 contributors, and Scalus.js reaches more than 20,000 downloads per month.
The proposal is a reduced resubmission from a previous ₳8.503 million, 12-month scope to ₳2.464844 million over 9 months with no contingency.
The funded scope excludes a standalone L1 node, full L2 integration, broad formal verification, and advanced devnet expansion.
Delivery is described as milestone-based and administered through audited SundaeSwap treasury contracts with an independent oversight board and third-party assurance.

Dijkstra hard-fork readiness is needed because Plutus V4, nested transactions, guard scripts, and accounts affect smart contract development, Plutus evaluation, transaction building, ledger rules, testing, and developer workflows.
Lantr Engineering says it has delivered every prior milestone on time and commits to public reporting, open community sessions, and on-time milestone delivery for treasury-funded work.
Scalus is presented as Apache 2.0 open-source infrastructure intended to reduce repeated assembly work across Cardano teams and tools.

summary: The document requests ₳2,464,844 for a 9-month Scalus continuation by Lantr Engineering, emphasizing prior adoption, reduced scope versus an earlier proposal, Dijkstra readiness, interoperability, and a first scoped runtime, but many adoption, governance, and execution claims are asserted rather than evidenced inside the anchor text.
